title: POC Weekly Sync - App Integration (SDK / Tool / Structured Output) - Arcadia Labs
summary: Weekly POC sync to review integration progress for application-level SDK usage, function/tool calling flow, and structured JSON output. Discussed integration bugs, schema mapping, latency trade-offs, and security/KMS requirements. Agreed next steps: share benchmark runbook, SDK snippet for tool-calls, and run latency test next week.
action_items: Maya Chen - Provide sample SDK snippet for function/tool calling (include retries + idempotency) - due 2026-12-10
Liam O'Connor - Run the 1k-conversation latency benchmark and share raw results - due 2026-12-14
Jordan Patel - Share Redwood security packet and KMS integration guide - due 2026-12-09
Priya Rao - Confirm list of 3 canonical structured-output schemas to lock for pilot - due 2026-12-11
next_steps: Redwood to send SDK example repo + gist for tool-calls
Customer to run latency benchmark and upload CSV to shared sheet
Schedule deep-dive with security team if KMS questions remain
Plan canary run on Redwood Dedicated if results look good
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-07 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Liam (Arcadia Lead Eng), Priya (PM), Ethan (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick check-in, hope the week has been good. we'll go through the integration notes and then hand off action items.
[00:20] Priya: thanks, Jordan. quick ask up front — can we confirm the demo flow from last week? the structured output piece was the blocker.
[00:30] Maya: yeah, so we pushed a small SDK update to help with function-calls. note: the sample uses the new redwood sdk v0.9.1, the function-call helpers are in redwood.tools.call, uh, there was a mismatch in the schema keys last time.
[01:02] Liam: right, on our side the app expected "patientId" but the model returned "patient_id" and that caused a deserialization 422. so we added a small mapper but we want a long-term solution.
[01:30] Maya: got it. we recommend defining a canonical JSON schema (we gave an example in the deck). we can add a small helper in the SDK to map common snake/camel cases, also include strict validation mode.
[02:10] Ethan: security note — how does the SDK handle secrets for tool-calls? we don't want keys stored in logs or transmitted to hosted endpoints.
[02:30] Jordan: yeah good Q. Redwood's SDK supports local KMS integration; we also have an option to use a customer-managed KMS for private deployments. i'll share the KMS integration guide after.
[03:00] Priya: can you clarify hosted vs dedicated for this POC? we saw better latency on dedicated in the benchmarks but cost is a concern.
[03:20] Maya: correct, dedicated lowers p95 latency and gives predictable throughput. hosted is cheaper for low qps but can have slightly higher p95. for your realtime workflows (sub-500ms target) dedicated is recommended.
[03:50] Liam: our target is 300-400ms p95 for the function-call flow, including the internal DB lookup. is that realistic?
[04:10] Maya: depends on batching and KV cache. If you keep sequence length small and avoid batching large requests, 300-400ms is achievable on dedicated GPU pools — uh sorry, dedicated GPU pools. we should run the microbenchmark with your exact payload.
[04:40] Priya: regarding tool-calls, we're invoking internal microservices for enrichment, what's the suggested pattern for retries and idempotency?
[05:00] Maya: recommended: client issues a function-call with a correlation id, retry on 5xx with exponential backoff, make operations idempotent server-side. SDK sample will include a retry wrapper and a small idempotency token helper.
[05:30] Liam: perfect. on the structured output side we also need to ensure hallucination checks — sometimes the model invents fields. any suggestions?
[05:50] Maya: yes, add schema validation post-response and a small guard rail: if required fields missing or confidence low, fall back to a safer path or call a simpler model. we can also add a verify step — send back the model output to a secondary verifier model, though that adds latency.
[06:20] Jordan: quick pivot to integration bugs you saw — Liam, can you summarize current failing flows?
[06:30] Liam: sure. two main ones: key mismatch (snake vs camel) which causes parser errors, and occasional 500s from our enrichment service during retries which the SDK surfaces as 'tool-call failed' with little context.
[06:50] Priya: the 500s happen during load spikes, we have autoscaling but the enrichment microservice has a cold start penalty.
[07:10] Maya: for the 500s we suggest async tool-calls for nonblocking enrichments — i.e., kick off a job and poll. SDK supports an async pattern. this will decouple the model p95 from the service latency.
[07:40] Ethan: about logs — we need audit logs for function-calls, and per-request trace ids. is Redwood able to provide token-level tracing or do we need to ship logs to our SIEM?
[08:00] Jordan: Redwood Console can show per-route traces and token-level timestamps. for audit logs we can forward logs to your SIEM via secure log forwarding and we support masked logs so API keys aren't stored. i'll send the log retention options.
[08:30] Priya: great. also, any limitations we should know about for structured output size? we have large payloads for patient notes.
[08:45] Maya: there's a tradeoff: longer sequence length ups token cost and latency. for huge docs consider chunking + streaming or embeddings + retrieval to reduce tokens. also quantization and batching profiles can help.
[09:10] Liam: we tried the SDK streaming mode but saw some hiccups — partial JSON chunks made our parser fail.
[09:25] Maya: streaming with structured JSON is tricky. recommended pattern: stream as NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) or stream raw tokens but finalize on the client with a reassembly step; SDK has helpers for reassembly in the upcoming patch.
[09:50] Priya: can you talk about function/tool calling with state? our enrichment requires auth tokens per-user to call internal APIs.
[10:10] Maya: store per-user tokens in your vault, pass short-lived bearer tokens to the tool-call layer. don't embed user tokens in model prompts. SDK will support passing an opaque reference and let the backend resolve it in your network boundary.
[10:40] Ethan: okay but does that change compliance? we need to ensure no PII leaves our VPC for pilot.
[11:00] Jordan: for Private deployments, the control plane can live outside but inference stays inside your VPC; we also offer on-prem for air-gapped. for the pilot we can enable VPC peering and customer-managed KMS so logs and keys remain under your control.
[11:30] Liam: sounds good. one more performance question — batching: we saw Redwood suggest auto-batching, but for realtime it seemed to increase p95. how do we tune?
[11:50] Maya: you can configure batching window and max batch size per route. for realtime set small window (2-5ms) or disable batching for certain endpoints; for throughput-intensive background jobs enable larger windows. we'll recommend profiles after seeing your qps distribution.
[12:20] Priya: on the SDK side we've hit a nasty bug where function-call return types don't preserve nested arrays reliably — sometimes turn into strings in our node client.
[12:40] Maya: hmm — that's likely a JSON.parse edge when streaming. can you share the exact payload and the SDK version? we'll reproduce and patch.
[12:55] Liam: i'll upload the sample request and the node stack trace to the shared folder after the call.
[13:10] Jordan: great. while we're waiting on that, Maya, can you outline the plan for verifying structured output correctness across the pilot?
[13:25] Maya: plan: 1) agree canonical schemas (Priya), 2) implement SDK validation hooks (we'll provide), 3) run regression evals on the prompt set nightly, 4) set up alerts for schema regressions tied to prompt sets. we can connect Redwood Optimize to suggest quant/metric changes.
[14:00] Priya: about regressions — can we get alerts when model rollouts change output distribution? we don't want to suddenly see new fields/hallucinations in production.
[14:20] Jordan: yes, Rollouts and Optimize tie into our evals and can do canary checks. we'll set up a canary with a holdback and auto-fallback policy if regression thresholds are hit.
[14:50] Liam: related: how does auto-fallback affect cost? if we fall back to a cheaper model, do we get cost offsets?
[15:05] Maya: fallback typically goes to a cheaper variant which reduces per-token cost. billing reflects the model actually used per request. we can show token-level cost breakdown in Console.
[15:30] Priya: scheduling: we need a security deep-dive next week to finalize KMS and SSO. is next Wednesday available?
[15:40] Jordan: yes, next Wed looks open. i'll propose a 60-min slot.
[16:00] Ethan: on data residency — we require EU-only data for some test patients. can we pin region for the pilot?
[16:20] Maya: yes, we can pin the deployment to eu-west and enforce region routing. for Private, all inference happens inside your region.
[16:40] Liam: ok, last thing — SDK telemetry. we want to capture error rates from the SDK but not the raw text. any privacy-preserving options?
[17:00] Jordan: we have masked telemetry; you can opt into tokenless error metrics, and full-text we only send if you opt-in.
[17:20] Priya: great. recap and next steps?
[17:30] Jordan: recap: Maya will share SDK snippet and validation helpers; i'll send security/KMS docs; Liam will run latency benchmark; Priya to finalize schemas; schedule security deep-dive next Wed. action items documented in the sheet.
[17:55] Liam: thanks everyone. we'll upload artifacts by EOD tomorrow for the mapper bug.
[18:05] Jordan: thanks all, talk soon.

Notes: transcript includes typical stutters and occasional mis-spelled product names (dedcated -> dedicated), and generic speaker attributions. References: "SDK gist" link placeholder, "latency-bench.csv" in shared drive, security packet link placeholder.
